purpose: VibeVoice-ASR front-end: stop freeing and reallocating the scratch arena on every encoder pass
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 256-bit LPDDR5X, 133 GB unified

protocol.weights: microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF acoustic and semantic tokenizer encoders + connectors, frontend_variant=wmma
protocol.change: _ScratchPool.reset() used to close the DeviceMemoryArena and create a new one on every call, so each encoder pass paid a hipMalloc/hipFree pair for the whole arena. It now rewinds the bump pointer when the existing arena is already large enough and only replaces it when a request does not fit. DeviceMemoryArena gains a rewind() method; the change is purely additive there.
protocol.why_it_matters: reset() runs once per encoder pass, so a forward is two resets. The requested capacity is 24 * chunk_samples * num_filters * 2 + 16 MiB, which is 287 MB for an 11 s clip, 754 MB for 30 s and 2.23 GB for 90 s (both encoders have num_filters=32). All resets within a forward request the same capacity, so reuse applies from the first pass onward.
protocol.method_primary: in-process rotating A/B: the same frontend alternates between the previous reset and the rewind reset, 2 warmup passes each, then 6 timed passes per lane alternating, so host drift cannot favour a lane
protocol.method_secondary: separate-process before/after on the same host, 1 warmup plus 4 timed passes per revision
protocol.command: python3 /tmp/frontend_ab.py (primary) and python3 /tmp/frontend_bench.py (secondary), run against HEAD and against the change

results.saving_scales_with_arena_size: 9.6 ms at 287 MB, 65.2 ms at 754 MB, 215.7 ms at 2.23 GB; the freed and reallocated bytes per forward are twice the arena size

output_bit_identity.verdict: identical between revisions for all three configurations, and identical across four repeated calls in each configuration, so reuse does not expose stale arena contents

gates.new_reuse_gates: 3 new unit tests: a fitting reset must rewind and not close; a larger request must replace the arena while a later smaller one must reuse it; repeated resets must rewind every time. All three are RED on the parent revision and GREEN after.
gates.embedding_identity: front-end embeddings are bit-identical before and after across 11 s single-chunk, 30 s multi-chunk (chunk_samples=160000) and 30 s single-chunk, and stable across repeated calls

notes: The multi-chunk case (30 s at chunk_samples=160000, three chunks) exercises six resets in one forward and still matches bit for bit, which is the case where a stale arena would show up.
Scoped to the front-end encode stage. In end-to-end terms an 11 s clip saves about 10 ms of a roughly 4.5 s pipeline, so no end-to-end claim is made.
benchmarks/README.md has no front-end stage row, so only the artifact and the changelog line are updated.
